processing: A clonal cultivar rather than a finished style; its leaf goes to both green and black tea in Hunan. Processing follows whichever tea is being made, and for green tea that means the usual fixing, rolling and drying.
harvest_season: Little is recorded for this cultivar. As with other Hunan garden teas, spring picking is the one that counts.
appearance_dry: No description specific to this cultivar is recorded; a green tea from its fresh, bright green medium leaf would typically be a dark green twisted strip.
appearance_liquor: Typical of Hunan green teas, a clear yellow-green; no description specific to this cultivar is recorded.
appearance_wet: Medium, long-elliptic leaves 7 to 9 cm long at full size, with wavy edges and a fresh green colour.
taste_profile: No tasting record specific to this cultivar is available. Expect what is typical of a Hunan green tea: fresh, vegetal and fairly full.

brewing.notes: General advice for a Hunan green tea, not specific to this cultivar. If the leaf was made as black tea, use boiling water instead.

vintage_note: Rarely sold under its own name; it usually disappears into regional green and black teas. As is usual for green tea, buy the current spring harvest and drink it within the year. A black tea from it would keep longer, as black tea generally does.
description:
Donghu Zao is a Hunan tea cultivar, not a named tea you will often see on a shop label. It is a clonal variety developed by selection from existing plants, and it is grown in the province's main black tea districts.

The plant is a small tree with a semi-spreading habit and plenty of upper branches. Its medium leaves are long ellipses, 7 to 9 cm by 2.5 to 3 cm, with wavy edges and a fresh green colour. It holds its old leaves well through a cold winter, but hot, strong wind can scorch the leaf edges.

Growers value it for yield, recorded at 11.6 percent above a widely planted comparison variety, and it is considered suitable for both the black and green tea areas of Hunan. Little has been written about how it tastes in the cup, so any tasting note here would be a guess. Treat it as you would any Hunan green: moderate water, not too long.

If you come across it, ask whether the tea is a single-cultivar lot and how it was made, because the name alone does not tell you whether you are getting green or black tea.
history: Little is documented about when or where Donghu Zao was bred. It is known as a clonal cultivar obtained by selection and spread through Hunan's black tea districts, and the breeder and date of release remain unconfirmed.
